NATIONAL INSURANCE COMMISSION
REVISED DIRECTIVES ON THE UNDERWRITING OF BOND BUSINESS
1.0 Introduction
The National Insurance Commission, pursuant to sections 2(1)(a) and
198(2)(c) of the Insurance Act 2021 (Act 1061), hereby issues these
Revised Directives to all insurance regulated entities to guide the sale and
underwriting of Bonds.
2.0 Scope
These Directives shall apply to all bonds underwritten by insurance
companies including:
1. Bid/Tender
2. Advance Mobilization
3. Performance
4. Retention
5. Counter Guarantee for Advance Mobilization
6. Counter Guarantee for Performance
7. Credit Guarantee
8. Suppliers Guarantee
9. Customs or Ghana Revenue Authority bonds including:
o Clearing Agents
o Warehousing
o Custom Petroleum
o Temporary Importation
o Removal
o Transshipment
o Re -Exportation
o General transit
o Particular Transit
3.0 Application Forms
The underwriting of all bonds must commence with the completion of an
application form. All insurance companies are to undertake adequate and
appropriate assessment of the bond application and all application forms
shall contain the following;
a. Personal Details of the Applicant
i. Name and Address of Applicant
ii. Email Address and Telephone No.
3

iii. Location of Office/GPS Address
b. Details of Beneficiary/Employer
i. Name and Address of Beneficiary/Employer
ii. Email Address and Telephone No.
iii. Location of Office/GPS Address
c. Contract Details
i. Full Description of the Contract Works
ii. Location of works or sites
iii. Total Contract Value
iv. Executed Contract Documents
v. Proposed Commencement Date
vi. Proposed Completion Date
vii. Maintenance/Defect Liability Period (where applicable)
d. Assessment of Applicant
i. Incorporation Certificate
ii. Company’s Constitution
iii. Three (3) Years Audited Financial Statement
iv. Statement of Affairs of Company
v. Board Resolution approving and supporting the Application
vi. Past Performance Records (Completed, Uncompleted and
Terminated Projects)
vii. Experience in execution of similar Contract
viii. Current Projects/Contracts being undertaken
ix. Directors and Managers Experience
x. Directors Financial Status
xi. Contract Funding
e. Bond Details
i. Type of Bond
ii. Bond Value
iii. Bond Period
4

iv. Beneficiary of the Bond
v. Past Bond Records
vi. Loss/Claims History on Bonds
vii. Facility Agreement from the Bank
f. Securities
i. Execution of Bond Monitoring Agreement
ii. Establishment of Escrow Account
iii. Counter Indemnity from Applicant
iv. Directors Personal Guarantee
v. Shareholders Personal Guarantee (where applicable)
vi. Appointment of Collection Bank (where applicable)
g. Waiver of Information
In limited cases such as Bid/Tender Bond Application, some of the
indicated details may not be necessary. However, if the contract also
requests for other Bonds such as Performance and Advance Mobilization,
then the information above shall be required.
4.0 Term Sheet
The assessment of every Bond application shall be initiated by a Term Sheet.
The Term Sheet together with the Application Form shall form the basis of
the Surety Contract and shall clearly spell out the terms and conditions upon
which the guarantee shall be issued.
The Term Sheet shall be signed by both the Insurance Company and the
Applicant to signify acceptance of the conditions in the Term Sheet.
See Appendix 1 for a template Term Sheet to be used by all insurance
companies for the initiation of all surety contracts.
5.0 Bond Wordings
5.1 Use of Standardized Default Bond Wordings
All insurance companies are required to use the standardized default bond
wordings at all times.
Insurance companies are prohibited from extending the standardized
default wordings to cover ICC/URDG/FIDIC rules.
The addition of the ICC/URDG/FIDIC rules completely changes the
interpretation of the standardized bond wordings.
See Appendices 2 to 9 for standardized bond wordings for all types of
bonds.
5

5.2 Use of On-demand Bond Wordings (ICC, URDG & FIDIC Wordings)
Insurance companies are strongly advised to exercise discretion in
accepting on-demand bond wordings.
Where an insurance company decides to use on-demand bond wording
(upon request by any Employer or Beneficiary), the insurance company
shall only issue such on-demand bond upon strict compliance with following
conditions:
1. The insurance company shall undertake a comprehensive
assessment of the bond applicant or application taken into
consideration all the requirements for underwriting of bonds.
2. The insurance company shall issue a Term Sheet that is signed by
the insurer and the contractor. (The Term sheet is attached as
Appendix 1)
3. The insurance company shall ensure that the On-Demand Bond risk
being processed is fully reinsured with reputable Reinsurance
Companies before final acceptance
4. The insurance company shall obtain collateral security worth one
hundred and twenty percent (120%) of the bond value from the
Applicant.
5. The Insurance Company shall obtain personal guarantees signed by
the Directors of the company in addition to the collateral security
6. If all the five (5) conditions above are met the On-Demand bond
application shall be submitted to the Board of Directors of the
insurance company by the Managing Director or a nominated
Management Staff approved by the Board and the application must
be duly approved by the Board by a written Board Resolution.
7. The On-Demand bond shall be signed by the Managing Director or
a nominated Management Staff approved by the Board of Directors
8. Any On-Demand Bond application with the bond value in excess of
Five Million United States Dollars (USD5,000,000.00) or its
equivalent in Ghana Cedis shall be referred to the National Insurance
Commission for approval after all the above conditions have been
met.
5.3 Default and Basis of Settlement Clauses
In respect of Performance Bonds, there shall be unambiguous Default
and Basis of Settlement Clauses to give clarity to the determination of
liability and the quantum of any claim.
The Default Clause shall provide for a Quantity Surveyor or Consultant to
assess the amount of work done by the Contractor at the time of default
and to quantify the amount of claim to be paid by the insurance company.
The Basis of Settlement Clause shall provide the settlement options for the
insurance company to settle the determined claim or loss.
6

5.0 Escrow Accounts
In respect of Advance Mobilization Bonds, Suppliers Guarantee, Counter
Guarantees, GRA Petroleum Bonds and Cocoa Bonds, insurance companies
are mandatorily required to insist on the establishment of Escrow Accounts
or into which the funds shall be domiciled.
The funds shall be released in tranches for use by the contractor on the
approval of the insurance company subject to a satisfactory report by the
Employer’s Consultant on the project or subject to a satisfactory report from
the Monitoring Team appointed by the insurance company.
Insurance companies are required to escrow all Advance Mobilization funds
above their Net Retention on bonds or Fifty Thousand United States Dollars
(USD50,000.00 or its equivalent in Ghana Cedi), whichever is lower.
For the avoidance of doubt, ALL advance mobilization funds in respect of
on-demand bonds shall be escrowed.
6.0 Monitoring
Insurance companies are required to have suitable and effective in-house
structures in place to closely monitor the performance of Contractors after
issuing bonds. Where the insurance company does not have the requisite
in-house expertise to monitor the bonds, the services of a competent third-
party shall be employed to do the monitoring.
In that case, a monitoring agreement shall be signed between the
insurance company and the third-party monitoring company or individual
with the requisite expertise.
The fee of the third-party monitoring team has been incorporated into the
premium rate.
See Appendix 10 for a sample bond monitoring agreement for this
purpose.
7.0 Rating
All insurance companies are required to strictly comply with the minimum
bond rates approved by the NIC in accordance with section 256 of the
Insurance Act 2021 (Act 1061).
See Appendix 11 for the approved minimum rates for bonds.
8.0 Underwriting Guidelines
All insurance companies that are desirous of underwriting bond businesses
are required to adopt and comply with the following underwriting guidelines:
9.0 General Underwriting Guidelines
i. Each company shall have clear written guidelines for the issuance
7

of Bonds.
ii. The Guidelines shall be approved by the Board of Directors of the
company.
iii. The signatories to bonds (authorized by the Board of Directors) must
be specified in the guidelines.
iv. Each Bond issued shall have a footnote clearly stating that the Bond
was issued in compliance with the Company’s guidelines
v. All bonds issued by insurance companies shall be in compliance with the
NIC approved market wordings.
vi. Each company shall submit quarterly report on Bond businesses
underwritten as part of the quarterly SDRs.
(See Appendix 12 for template of Report on Bonds.)
vii. Each company shall have the prescribed Term Sheet. The prescribed
Term Sheet and the completed proposal form shall form the basis for
the acceptance of all bonds. The term sheet must be made available
to all applicants.
viii. The company guidelines shall be periodically updated to recognize any
changes especially of signatories.
10.0 Specific Underwriting Guidelines
In respect of Advance Payment Bonds, Credit Guarantee, Counter Guarantee
for Advance Payment, GRA Petroleum Bond, Cocoa Bonds and Supplier Bonds,
the following specific Guidelines shall also apply:
i. Establishment of escrow account into which the contract funds and
receivables shall be deposited for monitoring purposes.
ii. Execution of a consent agreement between the Guarantor and
Applicant detailing how funds shall be disbursed.
iii. Execution of Directors and Shareholders Personal Guarantees of the
Applicant
iv. Release of escrowed funds in tranches in accordance with
the agreed milestones.
s
11.0 Sanctions for Non-Compliance
Any regulated entity that goes contrary to this Directive shall be sanctioned
for the maximum penalty units under the Insurance Act and shall in addition
be suspended from underwriting bonds for a period of not less than three (3)
months.

Appendix 5– Standard Counter Guarantee for Advance Mobilization Bond
Wording
THIS COUNTER GUARANTEE (“Guarantee”) is issued by
[Name and Address of Guarantor] hereinafter called the
“Guarantor” this day of 20 On behalf of ............................ [Name
and Address of the Applicant] hereinafter called the “Applicant” in respect of
[Description or Title of the Contract] awarded by [Name
and Address of Employer] hereinafter called the “Employer” In favour of
[Name and Address of the Bank/Beneficiary] hereinafter called the
“BANK” or “Beneficiary”;
WHEREAS:
1. The BANK is licensed by the Bank of Ghana to undertake banking business in
Ghana;
2. The APPLICANT has been contracted by the Employer to perform the Contract;
3. The APPLICANT has applied for an Advanced Payment Guarantee (APG) in the sum
of (Guaranteed Amount in words and figures) from the BANK to
enable the APPLICANT access mobilization funds from the Employer;
4. The BANK has agreed to provide the APG as applied for by the APPLICANT;
5. As a Condition for granting the APG, the BANK has requested the APPLICANT to
provide a Counter Guarantee to secure the APPLICANT’S obligations for obtaining
the APG from the BANK;
6. The Guarantor has agreed to give the BANK such a Counter Guarantee upon the
terms and conditions herein.
19

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS AGREED AS FOLLOWS:
We [Name of the Guarantor] hereby affirms that we are the
Guarantors and responsible to the Bank on behalf of the Applicant, up to a MAXIMUM
amount of (the “Guaranteed Amount in words and figures”).
1.0 GUARANTEED OBLIGATION
The Guarantor hereby irrevocably guarantees to pay to the Bank any sum not
exceeding the maximum amount of (Guaranteed amount in words and
figures) upon receipt by the Guarantor of the Bank’s demand in writing showing that:
a. The Applicant has failed to utilize the advance payment funds towards the
Contract or repay same to the Employer; and
b. The Employer has called on the APG; and
c. The Bank has made payment to the Employer in accordance with the terms and
conditions of the underlying Contract and the Guarantee Agreement.
IT IS FURTHER AGREED THAT:
a. In the event of a claim, the Bank shall first resort to the disposal of the Applicant’s
property used as Collateral Security and which is in their possession as well as
any money held in the accounts of the Applicant with the Bank.
b. The Guarantor shall not, in accordance with Section 255 of the Insurance Act
2021, be liable for any loss in excess of the said GUARANTEED AMOUNT and
shall not be liable for any damages penalties or other liabilities whatsoever of the
APPLICANT under the Contract.
c. The Guarantor’s liability under this Guarantee shall be proportionately reduced in
accordance with the recovery of the advance payment on terms and conditions
agreed between the Employer and the Applicant.
20

d. The BANK shall as soon as practicable notify the Guarantor of any circumstances
that may affect its liability under this bond.
e. The BANK shall have performed its obligations under the Guarantee Agreement
with the Applicant and non-performance of the APPLICANT was not caused by or
arose out of or contributed to by the BANK’s own default.
f. The Guarantor shall not be liable under this Guarantee if any change, addition to
or modification of the terms of the Guarantee Agreement is made without the
Guarantor’s consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, and shall
in such event release the Guarantor from liability under this Guarantee.
g. The Guarantor does not guarantee the performance of the APPLICANT under the
contract between the Employer and the APPLICANT.
h. The Guarantor shall have pari passu interest in all Collateral Security that the Bank
shall hold from the Applicant and such Collateral Security shall not be released to
the Applicant without the written consent of the Guarantor.
i. This Guarantee shall be read together and interpreted in conjunction with the
Guarantee Agreement dated and executed between the BANK and the
APPLICANT.
j. The BANK shall ensure the funds released from the Employer are paid into an
escrow account at the BANK and shall be released in tranches to the Applicant
with the consent of the Guarantor.
k. The Guarantor shall have the right to monitor the performance of the APPLICANT
under the Contract provided that the right of the Guarantor to monitor the
Contract does not in any way be a substitution of the BANK’s own obligation to
monitor and ensure the funds released are used for the Contract.
21

l. Any notice of claim under this Bond must be received by the Guarantor not later
than 30 days after the expiry of this Bond; otherwise any claim against the
Guarantor shall be rendered void.
m. Any dispute arising from the operation of this Bond shall be referred to arbitration
in accordance with the Alternative Dispute Resolution Act 2010 (Act 798).
2.0 NOTICES AND DEMANDS
Any demand made under this Guarantee shall be in writing signed by an
authorized officer of the BANK. Any such demand may be served personally on
the Guarantor or left at its address or last known place of business or sent by
post to that address. If such demand is sent by post, it shall be sent by courier,
registered mail or by hand and addressed to the Guarantor at its address or
place of business last known to the BANK.
3.0 GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION
This Guarantee shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws
of the Republic of Ghana.
